description: The bar chart illustrates the average number of likes received by posts grouped by their similarity to other posts, as measured by a metric ranging from 0 to 450, divided into five intervals: (0,90], (90,180], (180,270], (270,360], and (360,450]. The vertical axis, labeled “Avg. Like #”, ranges from 400 to 600 in increments of 50, representing the average number of likes per group. Each light blue bar corresponds to one similarity interval and is topped with an error bar indicating variability. The bar for the (0,90] group reaches approximately 585 likes, the (90,180] group is around 565, the (180,270] group is about 570, the (270,360] group is near 580, and the (360,450] group is roughly 575. The chart suggests that posts with lower similarity scores (0–90) tend to receive the highest average likes, while those in the middle ranges (90–270) show slightly lower engagement, and the highest similarity group (360–450) falls between the extremes. A gray square legend appears in the upper left, though no corresponding series is labeled, possibly indicating a placeholder or unused category. The x-axis is labeled “Most similar group of posts,” indicating the chart compares engagement across groups of posts with varying degrees of similarity.
